rich_summary: The Pandavas, aware that Purochana intends to burn them alive in the highly flammable lac house at Varanavata, carefully plan their survival. Yudhishthira reasons that fleeing openly would only make them easier targets for Duryodhana, who holds wealth, allies, and political power. Instead they pretend to live contentedly while secretly preparing an escape. Vidura, who had earlier warned them in coded language, sends a trusted miner who reveals the exact night Purochana plans to ignite the house and begins digging a hidden tunnel beneath the mansion. For a year the Pandavas maintain the deception. When the time comes, Bhima sets the house ablaze and the family escapes through the tunnel. Tragedy complicates their escape when a Nishada woman and her five sons, drunk and asleep in the house, are burned—leaving bodies that will make others believe the Pandavas have perished.

highlight_spans.why: Yudhishthira's cautious reasoning shows the political imbalance between the Pandavas and Duryodhana and explains why deception becomes their only viable strategy.
The arrival of Vidura's trusted miner confirms the conspiracy and provides the crucial means of escape: the secret tunnel.
The Pandavas' long deception—living cheerfully while secretly preparing—illustrates their patience and strategic discipline.
The drunken Nishada woman and her five sons unknowingly sleeping in the house introduce a tragic moral complication to the Pandavas' escape.

top_scenes.scene_text: A secretive miner kneels in the dimly lit lac palace chamber while the Pandavas watch as he opens the concealed mouth of a freshly dug underground tunnel beneath wooden planks.
On a stormy night Bhima ignites the lacquer house as flames race across the walls while the Pandavas and Kunti slip toward a hidden tunnel entrance.
Inside the banquet hall after Kunti's feast, a Nishada woman and her five sons lie asleep from wine while the ominous lacquer walls loom around them.
